cancer_indication: Breast cancer with RET fusions (metastatic disease; NCCN “useful in certain circumstances”).
moa: Selpercatinib binds directly to the ATP site of the RET kinase, preventing autophosphorylation and activation. In RET fusion–positive cells, this shuts off constitutive RET signaling that drives downstream MAPK/ERK and PI3K/AKT pathways, reducing tumor cell proliferation and survival. In ER+ breast cancer, RET activation is linked to endocrine resistance; by inhibiting RET, selpercatinib can restore sensitivity to endocrine therapy and has shown re-sensitization effects in endocrine/CDK4/6 inhibitor–resistant models.

KEGG_MEDICUS_VARIANT_RET_FUSION_KINASE_T.description: Constitutively active RET fusions drive downstream RAS/MAPK (MAPK/ERK) signaling.
KEGG_MEDICUS_VARIANT_RET_FUSION_KINASE_T.interpretation: RET fusion–driven MAPK/ERK signaling is a core proliferative pathway in RET-altered breast cancers and is a major downstream axis of oncogenic RET activity.

KEGG_MEDICUS_VARIANT_MUTATION_ACTIVATED_.description: Activated RET triggers downstream PI3K/AKT signaling that supports tumor cell survival and growth.
KEGG_MEDICUS_VARIANT_MUTATION_ACTIVATED_.interpretation: PI3K/AKT signaling is a key survival pathway downstream of RET activation in RET-driven breast cancer contexts.

HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.description: Cell-cycle transcriptional program driven by E2F-associated genes linked to proliferation.
HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.interpretation: E2F-driven cell-cycle activity reflects proliferative state in breast cancer models and is reported as suppressed in endocrine-resistant ER+ models upon RET inhibition.

HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT.description: Gene program associated with G2/M checkpoint control and mitotic progression.
HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT.interpretation: G2/M checkpoint regulators contribute to mitotic progression in breast cancer models and are reported as suppressed in resistant ER+ cell lines upon selpercatinib treatment.

PID_RET_PATHWAY.description: RET (rearranged during transfection) receptor tyrosine kinase signaling pathway.
PID_RET_PATHWAY.interpretation: Aberrant RET activity (fusions or amplifications/overexpression) can drive oncogenic signaling and is linked to therapeutic resistance (including endocrine resistance) in breast cancer contexts described.

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: RET fusion–positive breast cancers and RET-driven tumor contexts are described as sensitive to RET inhibition, with clinical responses reported and mechanistic suppression of downstream MAPK/ERK and PI3K/AKT signaling upon RET blockade.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: TP53 is frequently co-mutated in RET-altered breast cancer (~80%), inactivating the p53 pathway; the deep-research output associates downregulated p53 pathway activity with increased resistance.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HR⁺/HER2⁻ (Luminal A/B): RET is more commonly overexpressed in ER⁺ tumors that have acquired endocrine resistance. Selpercatinib shows activity in this context (ER⁺ endocrine-resistant models and organoids were resensitized), and NCCN guidelines recognize RET fusions as actionable in HR⁺ metastatic disease (RET fusion → selpercatinib).
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2⁺: RET genomic alterations have been identified in a subset of HER2⁺ tumors, though clinical data are limited. One index case with HER2+ breast cancer had a NCOA4-RET fusion and responded to RET inhibition (cabozantinib); the role of selpercatinib specifically in HER2+ cases is not documented.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Triple-negative (Basal-like/HER2-enriche: A majority (~65%) of RET-altered breast cancers were ER⁻, implying many fall into the triple-negative category. Data in TNBC are sparse; selpercatinib’s tumor-agnostic approval suggests any RET fusion TNBC could respond, but no TNBC-specific trial results have been published.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.BRCA1/2-mutated / HRD+: There is no known interaction between selpercatinib and BRCA status; no evidence links BRCA/HRD status to selpercatinib response.
